DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //ww•w dilg.com ph DILG OPINION No. 116 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 HON. MELVIN K. VARGAS Vice Governor Province of Cagayan Dear Hon. Vargas: This pertains to your letter dated 9 September 2022 concerning the Sanggunian's service vehicles. In the request for this Department's guidance, the antecedent facts are as follows: I. The Sanggunian Panlalawigan members were requested to turn over their issued vehicles to the General Services Office (GSO). 2. They were informed that the Provincial Accountant's Office will not allow the processing of gasoline expenses until and unless they attach a copy of renewal of Acknowledgement Receipt for Equipment which shall be issued by the General Services Officer and approved by the Governor. Hence the need to turn over the issued vehicles. 3. The turn over of vehicles to the GSO was said to facilitate the inventory and physical inspection thereof. 4. In view thereof, they cannot claim reimbursement for fuel expenses as there are no renewed or re-issued vehicles as of the moment. As such, they are seeking guidance on the following: 1. Considering that under the appropriation ordinance, the service vehicles are intended for all the members of the Sanggunian, may the General Services Officer or the Governor exercise his discretion as to who will receive the vehicles? 2. May the General Services Officer seek the prior approval of the Governor before signing the Property Acknowledgment Receipt for the vehicles? Section 375 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", states: SECTION 375. Primary and Secondary Accountability for Government Property. - (a) Each head of department or office of a province, city, municipality or Barangay shall be primarily accountable for all government property assigned or issued to his department or "Matlno, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

office. The person or persons entrusted with the possession or custody of government property under the accountability of any head of department or office shall be immediately accountable to such officer. (b) The head of a department or office primarily accountable for government property may any person in possession of the property or having custody and control thereof under him to keep such records and make reports as may be necessary for his own information and protection. (c) Buildings and other physical structures shall be under the accountability and responsibility of the provincial or city general services officer or the municipal mayor or Punong Barangay, as the case may be. (d) Every officer primarily accountable for government property shall keep a complete record of all properties under his charge and render his accounts therefor semiannually to the provincial or city general services officer or the municipal mayor or Punong Barangay, as the case may be. The foregoing legal basis considered, and in relation to the representation that there is an appropriation ordinance explicitly stating that the service vehicles are intended for all the members of the Sanggunian, it can be deduced that the primary accountability for said government property (service vehicles) is with the presiding officer of the Sanggunian being the head of the local legislative body. In this case, it is the Vice-Governor. The secondary accountability for said government property is with the sanggunian members entrusted with the possession or custody thereof Correspondingly, the Local Chief Executive (LCE) is primarily accountable with respect to the government properties assigned or issued to his department, he/she being the head of the executive department of the LGU. It follows, therefore, that on the ISt query, it should not be the General Services Officer nor the governor who shall exercise discretion as to who will receive the vehicles. First, in view of the governor not being the head of the Sanggunian and not the primary accountable officer with respect to the government properties issued to the Sanggunian. Second, the General Services Office/Officer should perform ministerial function with respect to inventory and physical inspection of the property and report it to the accountable officer, the Vice-Governor, for appropriate action. As to the second query, it is prudent for the General Services Officer not to seek approval of the Governor before the signing of the Property Acknowledgment Receipt for the vehicles. To seek the approval of the Governor is to put primary accountability upon himself/self for the properties that are to be issued to government officials who are not under his/her supervision. The Office of the Governor may instead be copy furnished with the pertinent documents in order to oversee the regularity in the performance of the General Services Office's/Officer's duty as the same is within his/her supervisory authority. With respect to the gas expenses reimbursement claims of Sanggunian members, the same is chargeable against the miscellaneous expenses of the Sanggunian's budget allocation subject to entitlement thereto based on limitations brought about by the public official's claim of Representational Allowance and Transportation Allowance Page 2 of 3

(RATA). Once a concerned official receives RATA, he/she is no longer entitled to claim a separate gas expenses reimbursement. The foregoing opinion is being rendered without prejudice to contrary opinion/decision of competent courts and/or authorities. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: VI OR LLAMAS ATTY. e etary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUS JVRULLLS-LRALLD/kbrn copy furnished: JONATHAN PAUL M. LEUSEN, JR.
